To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the projection onto a finitely generated cone can be reduced to two closely related projection onto the same bounded convex polytope and the least norm element of the convex hull of a finite number of points is found in an efficient way.

(1) the projection of a point onto a polyhederally convex cone generated by finitely many generators can be replaced with two closely related projections of this point onto the polytoe obtained by simple truncating the original cone, (2) this replacement is justified by the fact that the projection onto a bounded polytoe can be computed with the help of a specialized finite algorithm that significantly outperforms the general purpose quadratic programming algorithms when the number of generators exceeds the dimensionality,
the projection onto a polytopes generated by the finite set of generators can be solved with two closely related projections of the same bounded polytopes obtained by truncation of the initial cone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of finding the projection onto a finitely generated cone.

the development of a new approach to projection onto a finitely generated polyhedral convex cones, which is based on the projection onto bounded polytopes obtained by simple truncating the original cone.
a general problem of projection on finitelly generated convex cones and with the fundamental problem of least norm element in the convex hull of a finite set of points.

the proposed approach is a very promising and efficient tool for projection onto a convex cone.
our method is a promising and efficient tool for solving the problem of projection onto convex polyhedral cones.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the projection problem onto a polyhederal convex cone generated by finitely many generators can be solved by just two projections onto the same polyhedral set, which is a bounded polytope obtained from the original cone by truncation.
the proposed approach is very effective for solving the general projection onto a polyhedron, and it is especially useful for projection onto the cone generated by a given finite set.
we have found an algorithm for the general problem of the projection onto the finitely generated cone which is efficient and easy to implement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of projection onto finitely generated cones can be efficiently solved using just two projections onto a bounded polytope obtained from the cone by simple truncation.

the problem of finding the projection of a vector onto a polyhederally generated convex cone can be efficiently solved with just two projections onto the same polytope, provided that the latter can be efficiently found.
the projection onto the cone generated by a set of generators can be solved with the help of just two closely related simple projection onto the polyhedron obtained by truncation of the same cone.
